subject: New arrival dependent on the state of a variable

messages.author: a3c2c665afe78bd9
messages.subject: New arrival dependent on the state of a variable
parts:
Hi,
I am new to simmer but highly interested. I need to devise a simulation where one specific is that we can only generate new arrivals if a buffer is not empty. The state of the buffer depends on the previous execution of the process - i.e. we start with a full buffer, some steps deplete it some fill it up. At a given moment I want to strt a new trajectory, but only if there is at least one element in the buffer. Can this be done in simmer?

Thanks a lot for any help!!!
Kind regards

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] New arrival dependent on the state of a variable
parts:
On Tue, 11 Dec 2018 at 14:20, Sandor Bende <rog...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>
> Hi,
> I am new to simmer but highly interested. I need to devise a simulation where one specific is that we can only generate new arrivals if a buffer is not empty. The state of the buffer depends on the previous execution of the process - i.e. we start with a full buffer, some steps deplete it some fill it up. At a given moment I want to strt a new trajectory, but only if there is at least one element in the buffer. Can this be done in simmer?

There may be several ways depending on your specific needs. You can
set a global attribute (see ?add_global) and a generator that depends
on that variable (i.e., that spits out arrivals depending on the
reading of such a variable, see ?get_global). But you can also read
the status of resources (see ?get_capacity and subsequent functions in
the same help page). Another more sophisticated and more flexible
mechanism would be to set up a control trajectory with a single
arrival in a loop (see ?rollback). There, you can call activities that
apply a finer control over generators (see ?activate, ?set_source).

Iñaki

now I am trying the method of the global attribute as it seems to be the best for my needs. My problem is that I would need something like this, in pseudocode:

 Check number of  available clients
 IF number is greater then zero THEN

Another step in the process (trajectory) will independently increase the available number.

Is there a way for the generator to just release control and re-check after a while?

parts:
On Wed, 12 Dec 2018 at 11:18, Sandor Bende <rog...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,

> now I am trying the method of the global attribute as it seems to be the best for my needs. My problem is that I would need something like this, in pseudocode:
>
> Check number of available clients
> IF number is greater then zero THEN
> Release on client
> Reduce number of availables by one
> ELSE
> Wait until number becomes non-zero
>
> Another step in the process (trajectory) will independently increase the available number.
>
> Is there a way for the generator to just release control and re-check after a while?

No, this is not possible with a generator. As soon as the problem
requires some asynchronicity, as that's the case (i.e., the waiting
part), you need to control it externally from a trajectory using
activate/deactivate.

Iñaki

messages.author: a3c2c665afe78bd9
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] New arrival dependent on the state of a variable
parts:
I think I figured out a solution, what do you think of this ?

I have two types of resources "consumers" who reduce the buffer and "producers" who increase the buffer, both always by 1 unit.
I would define 3 global attributes, BufferSize, NextTake and NextAdd.

The BufferSize woud keep track of the size of the buffer.
NextTake is the time the consumer will finish its present job and will be able to process the next one.
NextAdd is the time the producer will finish its job and will be able to add the unit to the buffer.

The generator would look at the buffer. If it is empty it would return the time stored in NextAdd . That means that the consumer will need to wait until the next unit becomes available.
If the buffer is not empty then the generator wil return the time stored in NextTake , that is the unit will be released the moment the consumer becomes free.

The consumer always reduces the buffer by 1 when it starts and the producesr always increases the buffer by 1 when it ends.
Thanks a lot for your help!
